pages.title: Room Air Monitor
pages.text: An always-visible wall screen. Place it inside a sealed room; no menu is needed. Supply and demand use breathing-rate units: one Survival or Adventure player draws 1 unit. Creative and spectator players draw none.$(br2)In vacuum, sustained overload sheds ordinary flames, highest demand first after a ten-second warning grace. If breathing demand still exceeds supply after the flames are out, the room loses breathable oxygen while retaining gas, pressure and heat.

pages.title: Shared Supply
pages.text: SUPPLY and DEMAND describe the whole shared pool. LOCAL is this room’s demand. A Core touching two rooms shares one 8-unit output; it does not produce 8 for each room. Overlapping sources add once.$(br2)Sources must be inside or directly touch the room. Range alone cannot deliver air through unrelated walls.

pages.title: Reading the Screen
pages.text: Green: supported. Flashing yellow: at least 80% capacity, overloaded, or trapped air without production. Red: NO O2, no air or no seal in vacuum. NO O2 means sealed gas remains but oxygen is unavailable. Gray WAITING: geometry or consumer indexing is incomplete.$(br2)These are status and rate readings, not an O2 percentage. Room tanks and reserve-time readings are planned.

pages.title: Consumers
pages.text: Torch or lantern: 0.25. Each lit candle: 0.25. Fire or campfire: 1. Furnace, smoker or blast furnace: 3. Animals add demand.$(br2)Soul flames, Thermal Heaters, Returned and Architects draw none. Airlock reserves remain dedicated to cycling.$(br2)Comparator: 8 for strain/near capacity, 15 for no air/seal, 4 for no supply, otherwise 0.
Four iron, two copper, two redstone and one glass. The panel observes air; it does not manufacture it. ORSA advises against arguing with the numbers.

pages.title: Furnace Air Supply
pages.text: Furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces each draw 3 units. In vacuum, after ten continuous seconds of overload, one furnace pauses per second until demand fits.$(br2)A paused furnace uses no new fuel and holds prepaid burn time and cooking progress, even after a reload. It restarts automatically after spare O2 capacity can support its full demand for two seconds. Add supply or reduce other demand.$(br2)The room remains pressurized; a fuel pause does not cause a breach. Early ambient air needs no Core. Changing the input still resets recipe progress normally.

pages.title: Lights Out
pages.text: After ten continuous seconds of overload in vacuum, one ordinary flame block goes out per second, highest demand first. Furnaces draw 3 units; fire, campfires and MiteAway draw 1; each candle draws 0.25. Multi-candle blocks count all their lit candles together.$(br2)Torches remain as spent torches. Lanterns remain mounted but dark. Candles and campfires stay in place, unlit. Soul flames remain exempt.$(br2)Restored supply automatically restarts supported furnaces; other flames need relighting by hand. MiteAway retains unspent charge. Starvation preserves sealed gas and heat; it does not cause a breach.

pages.title: Breathing O2
pages.text: Flames shed before people lose oxygen. If breathing alone still exceeds the shared supply after the ten-second warning grace, the whole pool shows red NO O2. This is oxygen shortage, not a breach: gas, pressure and stored room heat remain.$(br2)Your existing lightheadedness, nausea and suffocation warnings apply. A working EVA tank or Emergency EVA reserve protects you. Add supply or reduce the crowd; support must stay adequate for two seconds to restore room oxygen. Saving and reopening cannot create oxygen. Early atmospheric air is unrestricted.

pages.title: Warning Cues
pages.text: A short chime warns when a nearby gauge enters STRAINED. The klaxon sounds only when you are approaching suffocation, after suit and tank protection are checked, even without a gauge. NO SEAL and NO AIR remain red visual warnings. Several nearby panels produce one warning per listener. Critical warnings repeat at most every ten seconds; there is no speech.$(br2)Near-capacity yellow alone is quiet. Combustion starvation is active. Breathing scarcity is active; room tanks and charging allocation are planned.
